Article Title: ‘No early warning’: Zelenskyy says allies failed to alert Kyiv before Russian strikes; Rubio says US intel sharing never paused
Article Text:
Zelenskyy says Ukraine received no early warning from partners before Russian strike

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy claimed that Kyiv received no early warning from its international partners ahead of Russia’s latest ballistic missile attack on Monday. The overnight strikes across 11 Ukrainian regions damaged more than 10 energy facilities and left at least 5,50,000 households without electricity.The comments come as US secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that the US had paused some intelligence sharing with Ukraine.The attack, which involved ballistic missiles and drones, also killed one person and injured eight others in Kyiv, according to local authorities. The strikes damaged residential buildings, a medical facility, a school and a metro station, highlighting the continued threat to civilian infrastructure as Russia intensifies attacks on Ukraine’s energy network.In a post on X, Zelenskyy said Russia had launched 16 ballistic missiles in what he described as a deliberate attack on Kyiv and the surrounding region, alongside more than 200 drones, including jet-powered Shahed drones.“Another Russian ballistic missile attack came in several waves overnight, and once again, there was no early warning from our partners,” he said.He added that the attacks extended beyond the capital, with strikes reported across regions ranging from Kharkiv and Dnipro to Volyn, Rivne and Odesa.“Overnight and this morning, Russia attacked energy facilities in the Vinnytsia, Volyn, Kirovohrad, Kyiv, Mykolaiv, Zhytomyr, Khmelnytskyi, Kharkiv, Ternopil, Odesa, and Rivne regions,” Zelensky said.“In this one night alone, more than 10 energy infrastructure facilities were damaged, and the lights went out for at least 550,000 families. Repair crews are working at the sites,” he added.Rubio on Monday denied that intelligence-sharing with Ukraine had been interrupted. “There's been no pause,” Rubio told NBC in Uzbekistan, adding, "I don't know where he's getting these things or why he's saying these things to the press. You should go back and ask him. There's been no pause."Ukraine’s Air Force said Russian forces had launched a large-scale overnight assault involving ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and 269 drones. Ukrainian air defences destroyed or suppressed 243 drones and four missiles, while strikes were recorded at 25 locations and debris fell at eight others, the force said.According to the Kyiv City Military Administration, the attack damaged a private medical facility and a metro station in the Desnianskyi district. Educational institutions and a sports facility were damaged in the Dniprovskyi district, while a fire broke out at a medical facility inside a 25-storey residential building in Solomianskyi district. Emergency services extinguished the blaze.Russia’s defence ministry also said it had carried out a “massive strike” using “ground-based high-precision weapons and strike drones”. It claimed to have hit military-industrial facilities, cruise missile storage sites and data centres in Ukraine, including locations in and around Kyiv allegedly linked to drone production and logistics.Ukraine’s deputy energy minister Artem Nekrasov said Russian attacks had targeted energy facilities in 11 regions. Rolling blackouts and electricity restrictions for industry and businesses had been introduced, he said in a post on Telegram.Zelensky also criticised what he described as inadequate support from Ukraine’s partners, particularly over air defence supplies and sanctions on Moscow.“Ukraine never wanted this war, and we have welcomed literally EVERY attempt by our partners to bring this war to a dignified end,” he said, adding that Ukraine had responded positively to every ceasefire proposal.“Putin not only doesn't want to end this war – he doesn't even want to take any steps toward de-escalation. EVERY ONE of our partners has experienced this firsthand when they heard Russia's refusals. And it is crucial to call things what they are. To call the aggressor an aggressor and help Ukraine defend lives. When deliveries of missiles for Ukraine's air defense are blocked while Russia is granted relief or delays in sanctions, this is, unfortunately, a denial of reality on the part of our partners", he said.
Article Summary: Zelenskyy says Ukraine received no early warning from partners before Russian strike. Comments come as US secretary of State Marco Rubio denied that the US had paused some intelligence sharing with Ukraine. The attack, which involved ballistic missiles and drones, also killed one person and injured eight others in Kyiv, according to local authorities.

Article Title: Tiger Shroff assassination bid: Why Mumbai Police can't get custody of Lawrence, Anmol Bishnoi
Article Text:
Tiger Shroff firing: Mumbai, Rajasthan Police arrest 3 accused

Why Mumbai Police can’t get Lawrence Bishnoi’s custody

Similar MHA order for Anmol Bishnoi

Security concerns and court appearances

NEW DELHI: Mumbai on Sunday witnessed another assassination bid linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, this time targeting actor Tiger Shroff. Yet, Mumbai Police cannot secure the custody of either Lawrence Bishnoi or his younger brother and close associate Anmol Bishnoi.A day after the firing incident targeting Jackie Shroff’s son, actor Tiger Shroff, Mumbai Police and Rajasthan Police have arrested three accused in the case. Mumbai Police are now expecting to secure their custody for further interrogation.The city has witnessed several high-profile incidents linked to the gang, including the assassination of NCP leader Baba Siddique, firing outside superstar Salman Khan’s residence and an attack outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty’s home in Juhu.Despite these incidents, Mumbai Police face hurdles in securing the brothers’ physical custody for interrogation in cases registered in the city. Lawrence is currently lodged at Sabarmati Central Jail in Ahmedabad, Gujarat, while Anmol, who was deported from the US in 2025, remains lodged at Delhi’s Tihar Jail.The latest firing incident has again brought the brothers into focus and raised questions over why Mumbai Police cannot take them into custody for interrogation.The primary hurdle is a ministry of home affairs(MHA) order restricting the brothers’ movement from their respective prisons.In August 2023, the MHA issued an order under Section 268 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), preventing Lawrence from being taken out of prison for any purpose. The order was initially valid for a year and was subsequently extended. The restriction was renewed under Section 303 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which replaced the CrPC.Section 268 of the CrPC empowered the government to prevent a prisoner from being removed from jail, overriding orders requiring the prisoner’s production before a court under Section 267. Section 303 of the BNSS provides a similar power to the state or central government, subject to the conditions specified in the law.The restriction has posed a hurdle for Mumbai Police, which has sought Lawrence’s custody in connection with cases registered in the city. In 2024, the crime branch approached the Union home ministry seeking permission to take his custody in connection with the firing outside Salman Khan’s residence.Police later sought his custodial interrogation in the Baba Siddique murder case as well.Lawrence faces multiple cases, including those involving murder, attempted murder, extortion and alleged drug and weapons smuggling, across states including Punjab, Delhi, Gujarat and Maharashtra. He is also in the NIA’s custody-related legal framework in connection with a case probing alleged terror funding to Khalistan supporters.The MHA restriction means that Mumbai Police cannot simply transfer Lawrence from Sabarmati Jail to Mumbai for questioning. Any access to him has to comply with the restrictions in force.The MHA issued a similar order for Anmol on December 5, 2025, barring police and investigating agencies from taking his physical custody for one year. The order requires agencies seeking to interrogate him to do so at Tihar Jail.Anmol was deported from the US in November 2025 and arrested by the NIA. He is a key accused in the Baba Siddique murder case and has also been linked to the firing outside Salman Khan’s residence.The restriction has created a similar hurdle for Mumbai Police in securing his custody for investigations in Maharashtra. Although agencies can seek to question him, they must do so within the limits imposed by the MHA order.Lawrence’s court proceedings have also involved security concerns. After his counsel moved an application citing a threat to his life, a special NIA judge shifted hearings from the regular courthouse to the NIA headquarters.Lawrence has also frequently appeared before the court through videoconferencing.With both brothers lodged in different prisons and subject to MHA restrictions, Mumbai Police face a legal and procedural barrier to bringing them to the city for custodial interrogation.
Article Summary: Lawrence Bishnoi faces multiple cases, including those involving murder, attempted murder, extortion and alleged drug and weapons smuggling, across states including Punjab, Delhi, Gujarat and Maharashtra. He is also in the NIA’s custody-related legal framework in connection with a case probing alleged terror funding to Khalistan supporters. Mumbai Police face a legal and procedural barrier to bringing them to the city for interrogation.

Article Title: ‘India is not Bangladesh or France’: Tharoor hits back at BJP, says opposition backs peaceful protest
Article Text:
‘We believe in peaceful protest’: Tharoor rejects BJP’s India-Bangladesh comparison

Political row over ‘regime change’

Tharoor comments on Musk's Starlink remarks

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Monday rejected comparisons between India and Bangladesh or France amid the political row over the opposition's use of the phrase “regime change”, asserting that the demand was for free and fair elections and not an attempt to topple the government.Responding to Union minister Kiren Rijiju's remarks, Tharoor said India did not support violence and that protests should remain peaceful. He also questioned the relevance of comparisons with unrest in other countries."I think that India is not Bangladesh and India is not France. I don't see these analogies as particularly relevant... We would never condone any of the violence, setting alight buses and police stations and so on, that has occurred in France. We only believe in peaceful protest... that's the kind of protest that I have participated in, and that I believe the opposition in general supports... As far as the larger issues are concerned, there's no point distorting a phrase like 'regime change' and so on. .. What we are calling for is free and fair elections... What is troubling today is that large numbers of people have been cut from the electoral rolls as the result of a completely troublesome, irregular, and partially illegal process.This is why we are calling for all this to be undone... It's a constitutional issue. It's not an issue of trying to topple a regime or anything like that..."Tharoor also defended citizens' right to protect democratic institutions, while clarifying that his criticism was directed at their functioning and not their existence."...Democracy is not a gift of anybody... we, the ordinary citizens of India, are the custodians of it... Every Indian citizen has the right to protect our democracy... All I'm saying is we are asking institutions like the Election Commission to behave themselves, to perform as they are required to by the democratic Constitution of India. That's all it is. I'm not in any way challenging these institutions as institutions. I'm challenging the way they are behaving, the way they are conducting themselves, and that is something that honestly all of us in India should be concerned about..."The remarks came amid a political exchange over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.On Sunday, Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju alleged that “anti-India groups” and some politicians had colluded to provoke young people and spread violence, claiming that a conspiracy similar to the unrest in Bangladesh and France had been planned in India.“The violent incident that occurred in Bangladesh and the riots, arson, and looting that took place in France, a similar conspiracy was hatched for India as well,” Rijiju said in a post on X.He further asserted that a change of government in India could take place only through elections.“Regime change in India is absolutely possible, but only through elections, not through Soros,” he said.The row intensified after senior advocate Prashant Bhushan described the agitation against Kumar as a “fight for regime change”. All India Students' Association (AISA) president Neha Bora also referred to the Gen Z-led movement in Bangladesh.Rijiju had earlier accused political rivals and activists of using street protests to create unrest and destabilise constitutional institutions. He said India's youth were focused on nation-building rather than political upheaval.Separately, Tharoor responded to Elon Musk's recent remarks regarding Starlink, saying the government had maintained that all companies bidding for the service were going through the same process and facing similar delays."I've heard the government's explanation on this issue, which is that there is a process and that all the companies bidding for this are in the same process and are facing the same delays. If that position of the government is taken literally, that means Musk is no further behind in the queue, and Ambani is no further ahead. I think we just have to wait for the process to play itself out... There are several factors. There are questions of the technology, certain security concerns, various kinds of details to do with the uplinking and finally cost.The last one, the ordinary public will decide. If you are giving me a service and he's giving it to me for 10 times the price, I may take it from you. Or if I really feel that what he's doing is worth 10 times the money, I'll give it to him. Each subscriber will have to decide. Personally, I'm quite happy with my regular connections. I'm not looking for a Starlink myself. But if there are people who feel these things are useful, in a free country, let them have the opportunity."
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor rejects comparisons between India and Bangladesh or France. He says India does not support violence and that protests should remain peaceful. The remarks came amid a political exchange over protests against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and allegations of irregularities.

NEW DELHI: The Opposition on Sunday targeted the Maharashtra government over the firing incident involving Bollywood actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai’s Juhu area, alleging that the incident reflected a deteriorating law-and-order situation in the state.Shroff escaped unhurt after unidentified gunmen opened fire near Pushpa Park on Sunday evening. His driver and an autorickshaw driver sustained injuries in the incident, police said.The incident prompted sharp reactions from opposition leaders, who cited previous attacks and killings while questioning the government’s handling of public safety.Shiv Sena (UBT) MP Sanjay Raut directly blamed CM Devendra Fadnavis , who holds the home portfolio, for the state’s security situation. Referring to previous incidents involving Salman Khan, the murder of NCP leader Baba Siddique and the killing of Shiv Sena worker Pradeep Purnekar, Raut said the latest shooting reflected a wider breakdown in law and order.“Devendra Fadnavis is the Home Minister of this state. He is also Chief Minister, but the responsibility for maintaining law and order lies with him,” Raut said.Calling the situation “jungle raj”, he demanded the government’s dismissal and the imposition of President’s Rule.He also urged the Supreme Court to examine the broader situation, alleging that shootings, murders, extortion and kidnappings had become matters of serious concern.NCP (SP)MP Supriya Sule also raised concerns over public safety in a post on X, calling on the state’s home minister to review the law-and-order situation.“Shootings are continuously surfacing across the state, and the situation is such that criminals no longer fear the law,” Sule wrote.She added, “In broad daylight, on busy streets, criminals are brandishing swords and firing shots. This picture of the law and order situation in Maharashtra is extremely alarming.” Sule said citizens were increasingly anxious about their safety and urged the government to take measures to reassure the public.Maharashtra Congress president Harshwardhan Sapkal also accused the Mahayuti government of allowing 'jungle raj' in the state and demanded chief minister's resignation on moral grounds.In a post on X, Sapkal questioned the safety of ordinary citizens, asking, “If an actor like Tiger Shroff can be shot at in broad daylight in a metropolis like Mumbai, then who will guarantee the safety of ordinary citizens?”"Law and order in the state has completely broken down. Criminals no longer fear the law, and the Chief Minister's control over the police administration has ceased to exist", he said in a post on X.Meanwhile, an FIR has been registered against three unidentified persons under Sections 109(1) and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), along with Sections 3 and 25 of the Arms Act.The Mumbai Police formed 15 teams to investigate the incident. Three men accused of involvement in the firing were arrested in Kota, Rajasthan earlier. Police are investigating the alleged roles of the accused and whether others were involved in planning or executing the attack.CM Fadnavis earlier said those responsible would be traced and would not be spared. Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde visited Shroff’s residence on Sunday night and assured the family of the government’s support.Shinde said, “Tiger suffered injuries to his left hand caused by gunpowder and glass fragments... Both the actor and his mother, Ayesha Shroff, were deeply shaken by the incident. Strict action will be taken, and threats against public figures will not be tolerated.”Investigators are also examining whether the shooting was planned after surveillance of Shroff’s movements.
Article Summary: Tiger Shroff escaped unhurt after unidentified gunmen opened fire near Pushpa Park on Sunday evening. Shiv Sena MP Sanjay Raut directly blamed CM Devendra Fadnavis for the state’s security situation. Opposition leaders cited previous attacks and killings while questioning the government's handling of public safety.

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor on Sunday criticised the Union government for not congratulating this year’s Nobel Peace Prize laureate, Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a South African jurist of Indian origin.The Thiruvananthapuram MP took to social media to question the government’s silence six days after Pillay won the award.“It’s been six days since this remarkable woman of Indian origin (see her story, attached) won the #NobelPeacePrize. And the Government of India, her ancestral homeland, hasn’t so much as congratulated her?! Shame on the petty men who have made such a deplorable decision,” Tharoor wrote on X.Without naming any leader from the ruling-BJP, Tharoor also drew attention to Pillay’s ancestral roots in Tamil Nadu.Navanethem “Navi” Pillay, a jurist at the International Court of Justice , was awarded the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize for her efforts to promote peace and international law by ensuring that war crimes, crimes against humanity and genocide are prosecuted.

NEW DELHI: As the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) intensifies its campaign demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, a group calling itself the Laal Hit Janta Party has emerged as a satirical counter to the outfit.At a meeting in the national capital on Sunday, the outfit called for constitutional values, accountability and responsible public participation, while reiterating its opposition to the CJP's demonstrations, according to a statement issued by the organisation.The outfit urged young citizens, particularly Gen Z, to engage in democratic processes through peaceful protests, factual communication and legal channels. Its motto is: “Nation First, Respect for the Constitution, Democracy as Our Identity,” while its guiding principle is: “Strong in Opposition, Peaceful in Action, Committed to the Nation.”According to news agency PTI, the meeting was held at Malviya Smriti Bhawan on Pandit Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Marg and was addressed by convenor Ayan Bhatnagar and filmmakers Richa Gupta, Pawan Nagpal and Atul Gangwar.The group's name appears to be a satirical reference to a popular insect-control brand, mirroring the CJP's name.The outfit had earlier held a gathering at Janpath, where around 200 people assembled to denounce alleged assaults on police personnel and abusive language directed at Prime Minister Narendra Modi during protests.Speaking to IANS, Bhatnagar had said the group was not formed to challenge the CJP through public debate."The Lal Hit Janta Party was not formed to contest elections, as we have already made clear. We stand against CJP and its protests. We oppose cockroaches who want to weaken the country's democracy and attempt to create anarchy in the country," he said."We will gather in different groups, on both large and small scales, present our views and arguments, and take our message forward. We will show them that a party like the 'Lal HIT Janta Party' now exists to challenge them. If you have the courage, come and debate," Bhatnagar added.In its statement on Sunday's meeting, the organisation said political debate over electoral processes should be based on verified evidence, transparent procedures and constitutional mechanisms. It also stressed the importance of preserving the independence and credibility of constitutional institutions, including the Election Commission, amid calls for Kumar's resignation.These developments come against the backdrop of widespread demonstrations against the CEC regarding alleged irregularities in electoral roll revisions. The protesters, including opposition parties, the CJP and several student groups have claimed that the exercise led to the deletion of lakhs of voters’ names and raised questions over changes to Form 6, which is used to register as a voter. These allegations, however, remain subject to verification.The counter-outfit called for questions about political organisations, their funding and alleged links to unlawful activities to be examined through verified documents, lawful investigations and official findings.
Article Summary: Lal hit janta party held a meeting in Delhi and called for constitutional values, accountability and responsible participation in protests. The group's name appears to be a satirical reference to a popular insect-control brand, mirroring the CJP's name. The outfit urged young citizens, particularly Gen Z, to engage in democratic processes through peaceful protests.

Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries.Shroff's driver, Firdaus, and another person were injured in the October 18 attack, which prompted a police investigation into the identity of the assailants and their motive.A message attributed to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing and linked it to Shroff's association with superstar Salman Khan. The message also warned others in the film industry against working with Salman.The attack is the latest in a series of incidents involving threats and violence allegedly linked to the Bishnoi network against Bollywood personalities and others associated with Salman Khan.The Bishnoi gang's message after the incident linked the attack to Tiger Shroff's professional association with Salman Khan. It claimed that Shroff had been warned earlier but had ignored the warning.The message stated: "Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next."In an audio message released after the attack, a man identified as Anil Pandit threatened Salman Khan and his family, warning the actor against relying on his security and demanding an apology to Lawrence Bishnoi and the Bishnoi community."Listen to me carefully, Salman Khan. If you don't apologise to my elder brother, Lawrence Bishnoi, or to the Bishnoi community, then we won't even leave a dog in your house. We will destroy your entire family. Keep this in mind. Don't think that you are in security and nothing will happen to you," Pandit said in the audio message.The message also warned rival gang members against using the group's name to gain attention. It appeared to be aimed at intimidating not just Shroff but others in the film industry who work with Salman Khan.The authenticity of the messages and the gang's claimed role in the attack remain subject to police verification.The dispute involving the Bajrangi Bhaijaan actor dates back to the 1998 blackbuck poaching case. Lawrence Bishnoi has repeatedly threatened the actor over the case, citing the blackbuck's religious significance to the Bishnoi community.The threats against Salman Khan have continued for years.In June 2022, a threat letter was reportedly found at Bandra Bandstand, where the actor's father, Salim Khan, used to go for walks.The letter warned that Salman Khan would meet the same fate as Punjabi singer Sidhu Moosewala, who was murdered in May that year.In March 2023, Salman Khan's manager received a threatening email referring to Lawrence Bishnoi's threats against the actor. The email also mentioned Goldy Brar, a Canada-based gangster and a close associate of Lawrence Bishnoi.On April 14, 2024, two motorcycle-borne men opened fire outside Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments residence in Bandra. The actor was not injured.Mumbai Police alleged that the shooting was carried out at the behest of the Bishnoi gang. Anmol Bishnoi, Lawrence's brother and a close associate, was among those wanted in connection with the case.Investigators examined the roles of the alleged shooters and their associates, including how the attack was planned.In a separate case, Navi Mumbai Police filed a chargesheet in 2024 alleging that members of the gang had been offered Rs 25 lakh to attack Salman Khan.According to the police, the plan included targeting him during a film shoot or while he was travelling to his Panvel farmhouse.The case also highlighted the role of people allegedly involved in surveillance and planning, beyond those who directly carried out an attack.The threats surrounding Salman drew further attention after former Maharashtra minister Baba Siddique was shot dead on October 12, 2024.Siddique, a three-time MLA and Nationalist Congress Party leader, was killed outside the office of his son, Zeeshan Siddique, in Bandra East.A social media post linked to the Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the murder and warned those helping Salman Khan. Police investigated the alleged links.On February 1, 2026, gunmen opened fire outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu.A post attributed to people linked to the Bishnoi network claimed responsibility and threatened further violence if its demands were ignored.Mumbai Police and the Crime Branch investigated the shooting, including the suspected attackers and their alleged links to the network.How the Bishnoi network operatesThe Lawrence Bishnoi network's alleged modus operandi involves different people handling the planning and execution of attacks.Police investigations have examined suspected surveillance, recruitment of shooters, weapons supply, communication between associates, and arrangements for transport and escape.In the 2024 case involving Salman, police alleged that the attackers had gathered information about the actor's movements and locations over an extended period. Investigators also looked into the roles of several people suspected of helping plan the attack.The network led by jailed gangster Lawrence Bishnoi has also been linked to attacks beyond India, including incidents in Canada and the UK.These include multiple shootings at comedian Kapil Sharma's cafe in Canada, which drew attention to the gang's overseas reach.In November 2025, news agency PTI reported that the National Investigation Agency arrested Anmol Bishnoi after his deportation from the United States.He was wanted in cases including the murder of Baba Siddique and the firing outside Salman Khan's residence.Anmol is Lawrence Bishnoi's brother and a close associate.Mumbai Police are investigating the firing to identify the attackers and establish the motive.Officers are examining CCTV footage and forensic evidence, while checking the authenticity of messages attributed to Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu.Investigators are also looking into whether Shroff had received any threats before the incident.The probe will need to establish whether the attackers acted on behalf of an organised group or whether someone claimed responsibility after the shooting to exploit the incident.For now, the alleged Bishnoi gang link remains under investigation.
Article Summary: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi's long-running feud with Salman Khan brought actor Tiger Shroff into the spotlight on Sunday. Seven rounds were fired in the incident, but the actor escaped without bullet injuries. A message attributed to the Bish noi gang claimed responsibility for the firing and linked it to Shroroff's association with superstar Salman Khan.

NEW DELHI: Unknown gunmen opened fire at actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday, injuring his driver and another person, an autorickshaw driver. The incident took place near Mumbai's Pushpa Park, within the limits of Juhu police station in the western suburb.According to police, the actor escaped unhurt, while his driver, identified as Firdaus, sustained an injury to his left hand."The chain of events leading to the incident is being pieced together," a police official said."Shroff is safe and has not sustained any injuries in the firing incident. His driver, identified as Firdaus, and another driver of the autorickshaw, identified only as Chauhan, were injured in the shooting and were rushed for medical treatment," the official added.Shroff and his driver were taken to Nanavati Hospital in Vile Parle. Doctors said the actor had sustained a few abrasions but no bullet wounds.The third person was taken to Cooper Hospital after sustaining bullet injuries to his chest.Meanwhile, Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility for the attack."Ram Ram to all the brothers. Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu take responsibility for what happened to Tiger Shroff today.We had called him and tried to explain things to him, but he did not understand. So today, we made him understand properly," Anil Pandit said in a Facebook post."Anyone in the Mumbai film industry who does not listen to us or works with Salman Khan will be next. Wait and watch."Note: And those dogs from other groups who think they can gain fame by using our name - we will soon kill them and make them famous."Salute to the martyrs," he added.The authenticity of the claims and their alleged link to the firing had yet to be independently established. Police are investigating the incident and examining the available evidence to determine the motive behind the shooting.Meanwhile, Mumbai Police has launched a manhunt to nab those involved in the incident. Specialised teams are examining CCTV footage from the area for leads."The incident occurred while Tiger Shroff was returning in his car. He was not hit by any bullets and is completely safe. Mumbai Police has formed multiple teams and initiated further action. The forensic team has begun its preliminary analysis, with approximately 15 teams currently working on the case," DCP Mohit Garg said."Further information will be shared as it becomes available. As I mentioned, the forensic team is carrying out its investigation. At this stage, it would not be appropriate to disclose specific details regarding the number of rounds fired," he added.Meanwhile, Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis called the Mumbai Police commissioner to seek details about the firing incident.He directed the commissioner to expedite the investigation and take strict action against those responsible.Fadnavis also called Tiger Shroff and spoke with him.He assured him, saying, “We are all with you. We will trace and apprehend the accused at the earliest.”Maharashtra deputy chief minister Eknath Shinde also condemned the incident and said Mumbai Police has formed several teams to track down those who opened fire. He added that the accused will be given a response in their own language."Tiger Shroff’s vehicle was targeted. This incident is deeply concerning and condemnable; I condemn it in the strongest possible terms. I have spoken with the Police Commissioner, and I have also spoken with Tiger Shroff. The Mumbai Police Commissioner has formed several teams to track down those who opened fire—they will be apprehended and given a response in their own language. Our current priority is to keep Mumbai and its citizens safe. Whether it is a celebrity or an ordinary citizen, ensuring their safety is the responsibility of the police and the government, and there will be no negligence in this regard," Shinde said."No gang will be spared; we will not let them get away with this. We have seen large-scale gang wars like this before, back in the 1990s. Even then, the Mumbai Police effectively handled the situation—they dealt with the perpetrators in their own language, ensuring that law and order were maintained. So, any gang attempting to spread terror here should think twice. This is Mumbai; this is Maharashtra," he added.Several personalities from the film industry have been targeted in shooting incidents in recent years.In February this year, five rounds were fired outside filmmaker Rohit Shetty's residence in Juhu. The Lawrence Bishnoi gang claimed responsibility for the firing.In April 2024, two men on a motorcycle fired five rounds outside actor Salman Khan's Galaxy Apartments in Mumbai's Bandra area.Mumbai Police arrested several suspects linked to the Lawrence Bishnoi gang. The trial against five accused - Vicky Gupta, Sagar Pal, Harpal Singh, Sonukumar Bishnoi and Mohammad Rafiq Choudhari - is underway. The sixth accused, Anuj Kumar Thapan, died in police custody in May 2024.
Article Summary: Unknown gunmen opened fire at actor Tiger Shroff on Sunday, injuring his driver and another person, an autorickshaw driver. The incident took place near Mumbai's Pushpa Park, within the limits of Juhu police station in the western suburb. Anil Pandit and Harman Sandhu, purportedly associated with the Lawrence Bishnoi gang, claimed responsibility.

JAMMU: J&K Police have filed a case and started a probe against a Jammu-based Army officer’s wife for allegedly collecting and sharing sensitive information with foreign intelligence operatives, including those linked to China, sources said Sunday.The woman is from Telangana, works as a freelance researcher and had a UN internship in 2023. Article Title: Sudden rain, poor crowd management likely led to Kolkata Durga Puja stampede: What we know so far
Article Text:
Locals blame sudden rain, narrow space and lack of police personnel for stampede

High-level committee reviews pandals

12 patients likely to be discharged on Monday

NEW DELHI: At least 19 people died and 25 others were injured in a stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening.The stampede occurred after a sudden downpour triggered a crowd surge, with hundreds of visitors rushing into the pandal for shelter and trapping those already inside.West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari blamed the incident on the organisers' callousness and appealed to puja committees across Kolkata to adopt safety measures.“It’s a painful incident and extremely heartbreaking,” Adhikari said.“As per initial information received, the incident happened due to an announcement made by the puja committee. Right now our priority is to treat the 25 people who have been injured. Among them, 24 are stable but one is critical. We are standing by the affected families. The Chorbagan puja pandal has been handed over to forensic teams, STF and fire brigade,” he added.Adhikari has also sought the list of temporary home guards deployed at the puja pandal to investigate their role in the stampede."These home guards are not new recruits. They were on duty for the third year in a row, following their earlier appointments in 2024 and 2025," he said."We are carrying on our shoulders a massive pile of rubbish as baggage. A clean-up will take time," Adhikari asserted.He pointed out that one of the home guards he tried to talk to at the pandal early this morning "could not even understand, let alone speak, Bengali".Here's what we know so far about the incident.Locals, who were among the first responders, said sudden rainfall, narrow lanes, a heavy rush of visitors and a lack of adequate volunteers and police personnel for crowd management contributed to the stampede.They said heavy rain forced people inside the pandal to wait for the weather to improve, while visitors outside grew restless and tried to rush into the already crowded marquee.Pramod Gupta, who lives near the Chorbagan puja pandal on Radha Madhav Lane, said the queue of visitors to the marquee had stretched to Mahatma Gandhi Road, about 700 metres away."Everything was fine till the rain started," he told news agency PTI."Standing in front of my house, I could hear screams as people rushed out. I and my daughters helped four girls and asked them to stay in our house till the situation eased," he said.Locals also said narrow lanes and a lack of police personnel and volunteers inside the pandal hampered the swift rescue of the injured."Ambulances could not reach the spot, and the injured had to be carried out to the main thoroughfare some distance away," a woman told PTI."We started the rescue work by breaking the bamboo structures and barricades of the pandal," another local man alleged.A high-level committee formed to review safety arrangements at major Durga Puja marquees across West Bengal began visiting community puja pandals on Sunday.The panel includes disaster management secretary Rajesh Kumar Singh and director general of fire services Anuj Sharma.The panel members will visit several crowd-puller Durga Puja pandals across Kolkata to review safety and security norms and crowd management plans, sources told PTI.The administration has stressed the need for wider exit points, adequate lighting and the removal of bottlenecks caused by temporary rope enclosures.Kolkata Police have arrested seven people, including organisers of the Chorbagan Durga Puja, a senior officer said.Police have also registered a suo motu case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder."We have arrested seven people. They were among the 14 detained last night. More arrests may be made," the IPS officer told PTI."Rajkumar Seoda and Shantanu Dubey were the secretary and vice-president, respectively, of the Chorbagan Puja committee. Biplab Mukhopadhyay was responsible for installing the bamboo structure at the pandal, while Kaushik Saha and Pintu De were in charge of crowd management," the officer said.Those arrested include the puja committee's secretary and vice-president, as well as two employees of a private security agency, among others, he said.The Bankshal Court remanded accused to 10 days of police custody. Police had sought 14 days of custody.Defence lawyer MD Yashim Raheman claimed that the accused were outsiders who had come to witness the Puja celebrations.He said the court had granted custody until October 28, while police had sought remand until November 1."We informed the court that these individuals were outsiders; they had come to witness the Durga Puja celebrations. Upon observing the heavy crowding--where many people were in distress--they stepped in to assist with rescue efforts...Regarding the police custody (PC), the court has granted it until the 28th. Everyone has been remanded to police custody until the 28th. The police had requested custody until the 1st, but the judge granted it until the 28th," he told news agency ANI.Authorities handed over the bodies of those killed in the stampede to their family members on Sunday.Among the victims was a 27-year-old nurse whose mortal remains were taken to her native place in Hooghly. Her relative told news agency ANI that she had gone to the pandal after completing her duty."After doing her duty, she went to watch the puja (worship/festival) with her friend," he said.The West Bengal government has announced compensation of Rs 25 lakh and a job for the family of each deceased person. The Special Task Force (STF) has also initiated an investigation to establish accountability.Twelve of the 14 patients admitted to Apollo Hospital in Salt Lake following the stampede are stable, with most expected to be discharged on Monday, Dr Narayan Banerjee said.Providing an update on the patients' condition, Dr Banerjee told ANI that five were in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU), while the remaining patients were being treated in the ward. He added that two patients continued to require closer monitoring.“Amit Shah ji came; it's a very good thing because the government has done whatever is possible. Except for two patients, all the others are stable. Of the 14 patients admitted, five are in the ICU, and the rest are in the ward," Dr Banerjee said."I think most of them will be discharged tomorrow, and a few who require surgery will remain here. Except for one patient who has a fractured pelvis and urethra, the others do not have very serious injuries or internal injuries so far. A young child, aged 13, was also admitted. She is fine,” he added.Union home minister Amit Shah and Suvendu Adhikari visited the injured undergoing treatment at Apollo Hospital earlier on Sunday.Shah had earlier expressed condolences to the families of those killed, describing the stampede as “extremely distressing”. He also said he had spoken to Adhikari to take stock of the situation.Following the incident, Kolkata Police imposed prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023, in parts of the city from October 18 to October 20 to maintain law and order and prevent untoward incidents.The order was issued amid concerns over possible demonstrations, rallies and meetings that could affect public order and safety.
Article Summary: At least 19 people died and 25 others were injured in a stampede at Kolkata's Chorbagan Durga Puja pandal on Saturday evening. The stampede occurred after a sudden downpour triggered a crowd surge, with hundreds of visitors rushing into the pandal for shelter. Locals, who were among the first responders, said sudden rainfall, narrow lanes, a heavy rush of visitors and a lack of adequate volunteers and police personnel contributed to the stampede.

Article Title: Almost a century after J&K HC was set up, Ladakh gets bench
Article Text:
CJI Surya Kant inaugurates the Ladakh HC bench in Leh Sunday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Almost a century after the establishment of Jammu & Kashmir HC, the Union Territory of Ladakh Sunday got a high court bench, which will sit in Leh, 3,500 metres above sea level — an altitude no other HC can ever match.Inaugurating the Ladakh bench of J&K HC, CJI Surya Kant said, “I am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher. Of course, what matters today is not how high this court sits. What is important is how close it now stands to the people it serves.”J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein.Speaking on the evolution of the justice delivery system in Ladakh in the presence of HC Chief Justice Pushpendra Kumar Bhati and SC judges, CJI Kant said given the difficult terrain and harsh winter, approaching the court was more arduous than the cost of litigation for many. Only after Ladakh became a UT in 2019 was J&K HC rechristened HC of J&K and Ladakh.“But a name on a court’s letterhead is not the same as a court on one’s doorstep… The high court has today crossed the passes to reach Ladakh, instead of asking the people of Ladakh to cross the passes to reach it,” he said, appreciating the efforts of Union govt and Lt Governor V K Saxena, who was present at the ceremony along with attorney general R Venkataramani.But even establishing an HC bench at Leh would not take justice to the doorstep of far-flung villages in the region, the CJI said, advocating liberal use of technology and legal aid services.“Access to justice, after all, begins not in the court’s compound, but at the litigant’s door. The law places this duty on the HC as well, through its legal services committee, and I am confident that, working... with the legal services authority, it will discharge that responsibility by reaching every door in Ladakh where justice is still awaited,” he said.In an unprecedented gesture, the CJI said, “Once video-conferencing facilities are adequately available to the lawyers of the Ladakh bench, Supreme Court shall list all matters coming from Ladakh on a single day, and hear them on a day-to-day basis, also through videoconferencing.”“Somewhere in Ladakh today, in a classroom in Kargil or Nubra, there is a young child who will one day argue her first case in this court, and perhaps even sit on its bench as a judge. When that day comes, we will know that this bench has not merely arrived in Ladakh but taken root here,” the CJI said.
Article Summary: J&K HC came into existence on March 26, 1928, with three judges, including Chief Justice Lala Kanwar Sein. CJI Surya Kant: “I am told no HC in our country has ever sat higher.”

Article Title: Menopause is normal, suffering through it shouldn't be
Article Text:
Is menopause in women treatable?

Indian Journal of Preventive & Social Medicine

When menopause symptoms are dismissed as ‘just ageing’

Treatment options for menopause range from hormone therapy and non-hormonal medicines to lifestyle changes

Menopause Symptoms Experienced by Women in India,

The doctor’s dilemma: recognising symptoms, choosing treatment

Is India’s healthcare system prepared for menopause?

Treatments available in India

How social stigma plays a role

Dr Soy talks to TOI

She lies awake at night. The next morning, she struggles to concentrate at work, snaps at loved ones over things that never bothered her before, or wonders why her own body suddenly feels unfamiliar.For some women, menopause arrives quietly; for others, it brings a wave of physical and emotional changes that can leave them exhausted, anxious and searching for answers.And often, the hardest part is not just dealing with the symptoms, but getting someone to take them seriously.Menopause is a natural biological transition, but the symptoms can be disruptive enough to affect everyday life. While some women dismiss them as stress or ageing, others find their concerns brushed aside or are unsure where to turn for help. Despite growing conversations around women's health, gaps in awareness, medical guidance and access to appropriate treatment continue to shape their experiences.A quantitative descriptive survey involving 150 women from urban areas assessed the impact of menopausal symptoms on quality of life. The study, published in the, was authored by Somibala Thokchom and David Ratna Paul Talagathoti.Participants aged 40 to 55 years completed the 11-item Menopause Rating Scale (MRS) to assess their symptoms and a modified 32-item Menopause-Specific Quality of Life Questionnaire (MENQOL) to evaluate how menopause affected their daily lives.The study found that 58.7% of participants were aged 40–45 years, while 75.3% had already experienced menopause. Overall, 92% reported moderate to severe symptoms, 4.7% experienced mild symptoms and 3.3% reported very severe symptoms. Nearly all participants (99.3%) reported changes in their daily routines.Although the findings cannot be generalised to all Indian women, given the small, urban sample, they highlight the potential impact of menopause on everyday life.The question is not simply how women experience menopause, but why so many may struggle to recognise their symptoms, seek medical advice or access appropriate care.Many women continue to experience menopause symptoms without seeking medical help, often assuming that fatigue, anxiety, disturbed sleep and mood changes are an inevitable part of ageing.Doctors say this can delay assessment and treatment, particularly when women prioritise family and work responsibilities over their own health.“Menopause is a natural condition, but that does not necessarily imply that symptoms cannot be treated,” said Dr Mitul Gupta, senior consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Cocoon Hospital, Jaipur.Dr Gupta cautioned against attributing symptoms to ageing without proper examination. Fatigue, irritability and poor concentration can also occur with conditions such as thyroid disorders, anaemia, sleep disorders and anxiety, making a detailed medical assessment important.Maya, a Uttar Pradesh native who now lives in Delhi, said, “I started experiencing menopause when I was 51. I did face difficulties, but back then, we didn’t really talk about these things at home. I used to feel hesitant."“I thought it was just a normal part of aging, and no one in my family really knew what I was going through. Even today, many families are unaware of what women experience during menopause, and often, women end up dealing with it on their own,” she adds.Menopause care extends beyond irregular periods and hot flashes. Hormonal changes can affect sleep, mood and sexual health, while the menopausal transition is also an important time to discuss longer-term health concerns, including bone health.A systematic review titledexamined 23 studies reporting symptoms among menopausal women in India. The review followed the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and included eligibility criteria, a literature search, screening and data extraction.The review found that somatic symptoms were the most frequently reported category, with an average of 73.66% across the studies. Joint and muscular pain and fatigue were the most commonly reported complaints, followed by hot flashes.Psychological symptoms were reported in an average of 63.03% of women in the studies assessing this category. Eighteen studies reported psychosomatic symptoms, while five did not report psychological symptoms.Urogenital symptoms were reported in 13 studies, with an average prevalence of 51.40%. Ten studies did not report symptoms in this category. Although urogenital symptoms were the least frequently reported, the review noted that women who experienced them reported greater symptom intensity.The findings highlight the range of symptoms associated with menopause and the importance of recognising them rather than dismissing them as an unavoidable consequence of ageing. The percentages are averages reported across the reviewed studies and should not be interpreted as prevalence estimates for all Indian women.Menopause symptoms can vary considerably from one woman to another, making individual assessment essential before deciding on treatment.Hormone replacement therapy (HRT) can help women experiencing troublesome symptoms, including hot flashes and night sweats, but it is not suitable for everyone. Decisions about treatment must take into account an individual's symptoms, medical history, age, time since menopause and potential risks.“HRT is neither universally dangerous nor suitable for everyone. The right treatment is the one that is carefully chosen according to your individual needs, with proper medical guidance and regular follow-up,” said Dr Bharti Soy, consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Fortis O.P. Jindal Hospital & Research Centre.Doctors emphasise that consultations should cover the potential benefits and risks of hormone therapy, as well as non-hormonal alternatives where appropriate. Women should be able to discuss their concerns and make informed decisions with their healthcare providers.Symptoms should not automatically be attributed to menopause, as other medical conditions may require separate investigation and treatment. A thorough consultation can help distinguish between menopause-related changes and other possible causes, allowing care to be tailored to the individual's needs.Awareness alone may not be enough if women cannot access appropriate and affordable care. Gaps in menopause-specific knowledge, counselling and healthcare access can leave women without adequate guidance on managing their symptoms.The challenge is not limited to the availability of gynaecologists, but also whether consultations address menopause-related concerns beyond menstrual changes. Symptoms affecting sleep, mood, sexual wellbeing and bone health may require a broader discussion of a woman's physical and emotional health.“Women need a complete evaluation not a consultation for the issues related to menstruation,” said Dr Priyanka Sharma, senior consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Cocoon Hospital, Chandigarh.Barriers such as the cost of travel, time away from work, lack of awareness and limited access to healthcare facilities can make seeking care more difficult. Strengthening primary-level assessment, training healthcare workers and establishing referral pathways could help women receive appropriate support.Education in local languages and more affordable treatment options are also important to ensure that women can understand their symptoms, discuss available choices and access care when needed.Making menopause a routine part of women's healthcare could help shift the focus from simply enduring symptoms to identifying and managing them appropriately.Medical care is only part of the picture. Family attitudes and social expectations can influence whether women feel comfortable discussing menopause or seeking help.“In many Indian households, menopause is still not discussed openly because of social stigma, lack of awareness, and the belief that it is simply a natural process. As a result, many women suffer silently rather than seeking medical help,” said Dr Bharti Soy.When symptoms such as disturbed sleep, irritability or discomfort are dismissed as inevitable consequences of growing older, women may begin to question whether their concerns deserve medical attention.“If relatives tell her that discomfort, irritability or sleep problems are simply part of growing older, she may question whether her concerns deserve medical attention,” said Dr Swati Sinha, senior consultant, obstetrics and gynaecology, Rosewalk by Rainbow Hospitals.Families can help by making menopause a subject that can be discussed without embarrassment or judgement. Listening without dismissing symptoms, offering practical support and encouraging medical consultations when problems affect daily life can make the transition easier to navigate.Partners, children and other family members need not have all the answers. Understanding that menopause affects women differently, and that help is available when symptoms become disruptive, is an important first step.Menopause may be a natural stage of life, but that does not mean women should have to endure its more difficult symptoms without support. Better awareness, informed medical consultations, accessible treatment and understanding families can help ensure that women are heard and their concerns taken seriously.
Article Summary: Menopause can bring a range of physical, emotional and urogenital symptoms. Treatment options for menopause range from hormone therapy and non-hormonal medicines to lifestyle changes. Despite growing conversations around women's health, gaps in awareness, medical guidance and access to appropriate treatment continue to shape their experiences.

Article Title: 'Barged in, cut power': AAP's Saurabh Bharadwaj claims Delhi Police harassing Bengali community in CR Park

NEW DELHI: Saurabh Bharadwaj has accused Delhi Police of harassing the Bengali community and Durga Puja committees in Chittaranjan Park (CR Park), alleging that police personnel forcibly disconnected electricity at a pandal and damaged equipment. He also warned that restrictions on Puja celebrations could lead to overcrowding, drawing a parallel with the Kolkata stampede that killed 17 people on Saturday.In a post on X addressed to Delhi Lieutenant Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) state president claimed that the community and Puja organisers were facing unprecedented harassment.“Attention @LtGovDelhi saab, Delhi Police officers are harassing the Bengali community and CR Park Durga Puja Committees like never before. This community is one of the most decent and well-educated sections of Delhi,” he wrote.Questioning the alleged disparity in the treatment of different cultural events, Bharadwaj referred to the Delhi government's position on allowing shops and businesses to operate round the clock and said most Ram Leela celebrations were permitted to continue past midnight.“When the Delhi Govt talks about 24x7 businesses and shops, and most Ram-leelas are allowed past midnight, why the stepmotherly treatment for the Bengali community?” he asked.Bharadwaj also alleged that police constables entered the B Block Durga Puja pandal on Saturday and cut its electricity connections. “Yesterday, police constables barged into the B Block Durga Puja pandal and forcibly cut the electrical connections, damaging their equipment. This is not done,” he said.In another post on X, Bharadwaj criticised the BJP over the reported West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy and raised concerns about crowd management at the Puja pandals.“BJP has learnt nothing from the West Bengal Durga Puja tragedy,” he wrote.He claimed that lakhs of people, including Bengalis and non-Bengalis, visit CR Park's Puja pandals every year, particularly in the evenings. He further alleged that Puja committees had been told that pandals and loudspeakers could operate only until 10 pm this year, compared with midnight last year.“Squeezing the evening window by 2 hours will cause crowd swell and chaos. This could lead to a West Bengal-type situation, and the government will prosecute puja committees to hide its own shortcomings,” Bharadwaj alleged.Meanwhile, the Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions in CR Park, Greater Kailash-II and adjoining areas of South Delhi from October 16 to 20, between 4 pm and midnight, citing the expected influx of visitors and limited road space around the pandals.Private vehicles belonging to visitors and devotees will not be allowed to enter CR Park and Greater Kailash-II during the restricted hours. Commuters have been advised to use the Delhi Metro, with taxi and auto-rickshaw drop-off points designated at Greater Kailash and Nehru Enclave Metro stations. The police has also warned that illegally parked vehicles or those obstructing traffic may be towed and prosecuted.The restrictions are scheduled to remain in place until October 20.
Article Summary: Saurabh Bharadwaj accuses Delhi Police of harassing the Bengali community and Durga Puja committees in Chittaranjan Park (CR Park) He alleges that police personnel forcibly disconnected electricity at a pandal and damaged equipment. Delhi Traffic Police has announced restrictions in CR Park, Greater Kailash-II and adjoining areas of South Delhi from October 16 to 20.

Article Title: Centre issues advisory to Meta, asks it to overhaul content promotion system on Facebook, Instagram
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta, which owns Instagram and Facebook, to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives. ""Ensure that recommendation systems do not result in disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives, and endeavour to provide appropriate diversity of relevant and credible information," an advisory issued by the ministry of electronics and information technology (MeitY), dated October 10, stated, PTI reported."Also strengthen mechanisms for rapid identification, review and escalation of content, which is gaining significant reach through recommendation systems and has the potential to cause widespread public confusion, apprehension, violence or disturbance of public order," it added.While the advisory does not cite any specific incident that led to its issuance, it comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.MeitY also asked Meta to cooperate with law enforcement and other authorised government agencies by providing information or assistance within the timelines prescribed under the IT Rules, 2021.The ministry noted that certain content relating to "ongoing public events" was being "prominently displayed and recommended to users" on Meta platforms.Citing the Information Technology Act, 2000, the advisory highlighted the company’s obligation to exercise due diligence under the IT Rules, 2021, which require intermediaries to inform users about prohibited content, including material likely to cause public disorder or incite a cognisable offence.MeitY also flagged content presenting old or selectively edited visuals as current events, misleading claims about emergencies, restrictions or police action, and audio-visual material depicting law-and-order situations without adequate context. It also raised concerns over content likely to incite violence and misleading material receiving disproportionate amplification.The advisory outlined six requirements for Meta, including measures to identify and address prohibited content and review recommendation and ranking systems to ensure misleading, manipulated or out-of-context material is not "disproportionately amplified or repeatedly recommended to users".MeitY emphasised that the advisory seeks to promote responsible information dissemination while respecting lawful expression and public discourse."Meta is advised to ensure that any action taken pursuant to this advisory is consistent with the Information Technology Act, 2000, the IT Rules, 2021, and other applicable laws," the ministry added.
Article Summary: The Centre has directed social media giant Meta to ensure that its recommendation algorithms do not result in "disproportionate exposure of users to a single or limited set of narratives" It comes amid ongoing protests in Delhi demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

Article Title: Bimol Akoijam willing to contest Manipur Assembly polls if Congress offers ticket
Article Text:
File photo: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam

JNU dismissal and police investigation

Akoijam says Manipur's wider crisis needs attention

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam on Sunday said he was willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from the Keishamthong constituency if the party offered him a ticket, as he faces a sexual harassment case and has been dismissed from Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).Speaking at an event, the Inner Manipur MP said his decision to enter the electoral contest would be guided by the future of the state."I am ready to fight elections from Keishamthong (in Imphal West district). If the party offers me a ticket, I will contest the Keisamthong assembly constituency. This decision is for the future of the state," Akoijam said, according to news agency PTI.The Manipur Assembly elections are due next year.His remarks come amid an ongoing police investigation into sexual harassment allegations against him and his dismissal from JNU, where he was a professor at the Centre for the Study of Social Systems under the School of Social Sciences.Akoijam was dismissed from the university on October 9 following an inquiry into allegations of sexual harassment. He has denied the charges and described the university's action as a "witch hunt", claiming he was not given an opportunity to respond to the inquiry committee's findings.Delhi Police booked him on October 11 following a complaint by JNU's chief security officer. He recently appeared before investigators at the Vasant Kunj North Police Station in New Delhi in connection with the case.At least 11 female students submitted complaints against Akoijam in May. They alleged that he invited students to his campus residence on the pretext of meetings or gatherings and attempted to harass them. Some students also alleged that he made obscene and inappropriate remarks in class.After appearing before investigators, Akoijam said he intended to challenge his dismissal legally.Speaking to reporters in Imphal on Friday, he said his lawyers were preparing the case and that he would file it within a day or two.He also said he had cooperated with the police and would continue to do so, while requesting adequate notice for any further questioning because of his responsibilities as an MP.During his remarks to the media, Akoijam also urged greater attention to the wider situation in Manipur, including the plight of internally displaced people, lawlessness and issues surrounding buffer zones."Thousands of people are languishing in relief camps. I don’t think my pain is anything greater than the pain of these people," he said, while alleging that the action against him was an attempt to silence his voice.The MP had earlier said, "Justice will be done," before travelling to New Delhi to join the police investigation.The allegations have also triggered political reactions in the state. BJP workers staged a protest outside Congress Bhavan in Imphal, demanding Akoijam's resignation and accusing him of bringing disrepute to Manipur. Police prevented the protesters from entering the premises.Congress spokesperson Hareshwar Goshwami described the protest as a diversionary tactic and accused the ruling party of deflecting attention from killings and the crisis in the state.Akoijam has maintained that the allegations against him are false and has challenged the process that led to his dismissal. The sexual harassment allegations remain under investigation.
Article Summary: Angomcha Bimol Akoijam says he is willing to contest next year's Manipur Assembly elections from Keishamthong constituency. His remarks come amid an ongoing police investigation into sexual harassment allegations against him and his dismissal from Jawaharlal Nehru University. He has denied the charges and described the university's action as a "witch hunt"

Article Text:
Union minister Chirag Paswan

NEW DELHI: Union minister Chirag Paswan on Sunday reacted to the ‘Leave India’ notice issued to actor Imran Khan over his participation in protests seeking the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Paswan termed the involvement of foreign nationals in India’s internal affairs “unacceptable”, while expressing support for peaceful protests by Indian citizens.“There is no objection to Indian citizens playing a role in matters concerning India while living within the country. I have always supported peaceful protests. However, I do not consider it justifiable for someone who is not an Indian citizen to intervene in India's internal affairs or play a role in such matters,” he told news agency ANI.“For someone who is not an Indian citizen to involve themselves in India's internal affairs—especially when there are growing concerns that foreign forces may be involved in orchestrating these events—is unacceptable,” the Union minister added.Paswan’s remarks follow the issuance of a ‘Leave India’ notice to Imran Khan by Mumbai Police on Thursday. The notice directs the actor to leave India by October 28. According to ANI, Khan, the nephew of actor Aamir Khan, holds an American passport.Authorities have initiated action against him under Sections 29 and 7 of the Immigration Act over allegations that he participated in a protest despite not being an Indian citizen.Khan had joined a demonstration at Mumbai’s August Kranti Maidan, where protesters demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He was detained by Mumbai Police last week.After his detention, the actor posted a picture of himself apparently sitting inside a police van, with the caption, “Apparently I’m going for a drive.”Khan said he had visited the protest site as a citizen of Mumbai and was not there to press any specific demands. He also raised questions about freedom of movement and what he described as the suppression of people’s voices.On Saturday, Khan approached the Bombay high court, challenging the notice issued by the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) over alleged violations of the Foreigners Act. His lawyer indicated that the notice would be contested in court.Earlier, Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leader Kirit Somaiya had called for Khan’s immediate arrest and deportation, alleging violations of Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) provisions and visa conditions.
Article Summary: Union minister Chirag Paswan says involvement of foreign nationals in India's internal affairs is 'unacceptable' Paswan's remarks follow the 'Leave India' notice issued to actor Imran Khan over his participation in protests. Khan, nephew of actor Aamir Khan, holds an American passport. He was detained by Mumbai Police last week.
